newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Portworker unions must decide on Brazil strike-fed.
newsitem.headline: Portworker unions must decide on Brazil strike-fed.

text.p: Brazil's National Portworkers' Federation is suggesting affiliated members support stevedores in a planned 24-hour national strike but the decision to strike is up to each union, the federation president said.
"The guideline from the federation is that portworkers accompany stevedores in a show of support and stop work at all ports," Jose Peres Cesar said.
"But we cannot force unions to go on strike. Each union must take its own decision," he added.
The Stevedores Federation has called for a nationwide strike from 0700 local/1000 GMT on April 4.
The strike is to show dissatisfaction with the progress of the government's port privatisation program.

Stevedores at the port of Santos have been striking since 0700 local April 2 in protest at a ruling allowing workers from steel mill Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa) CSL.SA to carry out loading and unloading at Cosipa's terminal.
Union officials argue that under federal law, only registered and qualified workers should conduct such operations.
Portworker federation officials have already said that even if members did not actually join the stevedores' strike, ports would effectively be paralysed anyway.
Cesar said that it would be only clear tomorrow how many unions affiliated to his federation had decided to particpate in the stoppage.
The strike in Santos has been affecting loading of key commodities such as soybeans.
Stevedores at Brazil's principal soybean port of Paranagua are today voting to decide whether to take part in the nationwide stoppage on Friday.
